title: customer-opt-in-replay-checklist-and-timestamped-evidence-2029-02-28
body:
Purpose
This draft is a compact customer-facing package to offer tenants the option to opt in to a replay of affected inference requests so they can verify integrity, reproduce outputs, or collect evidence for audits. The tone should be plain-language, low-friction, and emphasize data minimization and controls.

Status summary (short for status page)
TL;DR: On 2029-02-20 we observed an intermittent cache-eviction race that affected a subset of streamed responses for tenants in eu-west-1 over a 7-hour window. Most requests completed successfully; a small percentage returned stale or truncated structured outputs. We're offering an opt-in replay and a timestamped evidence bundle for customers who want a forensic replay or independent verification.

What happened (customer-friendly)
- When: 2029-02-20 02:15–09:20 UTC (impact window; rolling).
- Where: eu-west-1 serving tier; a minority of tenants using streaming + structured output features.
- Impact: Some streaming sessions produced truncated or stale fields in JSON-like structured outputs. Free-text completions were unaffected for the majority of requests. No customer data exfiltration occurred; only inference outputs were impacted.
- Root cause (summary): A concurrency race between our KV cache eviction and a new prefix-prefetch optimization caused occasional misalignment of the KV cache state used during token generation, which produced shortened or repeated structured tokens. Full technical root cause in the postmortem.

What we did immediately
- Identified a safe rollback of the prefix-prefetch optimization and removed the changes from the eu-west-1 fleet by 2029-02-20 10:20 UTC.
- Scoped affected tenants and traced sessions via request IDs and per-tenant routing logs.
- Enabled an emergency guard that prevents cache eviction during active streaming sessions.
- Began collecting evidence bundles for tenants that request replays (see opt-in flow).

Why we are offering a replay (why customers might care)
- Replays let you: confirm that outputs you observed were transient, assemble a timestamped set of outputs for compliance, or reproduce an endpoint-level behavior for debugging.
- Replays use the same pinned model version and recorded inputs; they are executed in an isolated verification environment and are read-only with respect to your data.

Replay opt-in checklist (customer instructions)
1) Decide scope: choose one of the options below and list up to 10 representative request IDs or a time range (max 7 hours) to replay.
   - Representative sample (recommended): 5–10 request IDs that exhibited the issue.
   - Full window (audit): entire tenant window between X and Y (note: may take longer and could include high volume).
2) Data handling consent: by opting in you acknowledge Redwood will reprocess the listed inputs in an isolated environment solely to reproduce outputs; no outputs will be used for model training.
3) Choose delivery: evidence bundle via secure S3 link (encrypted) or shared audit session with a Redwood engineer.
4) Optional redaction: you can request partial redaction of inputs (we'll redact to the minimal necessary fields) — indicate fields to redact in your reply.
5) Expected timeline: small sample replays within 48 hours; full-window replays may take 3–7 business days depending on volume.

What the evidence bundle includes
- Timestamped request logs (request IDs, client timestamps, route, model version).
- Raw inputs used for replay (redacted on request).
- Replayed outputs (generated in verification environment) with identical runtime parameters.
- Operator notes: which runtime knobs changed during the replay, any divergences observed, and a short conclusion.
- SHA256 manifests of each file and an overall signed summary.

Security & privacy notes (customer-facing)
- Replays occur in an isolated environment with no external network egress.
- Inputs are processed only to the extent necessary to reproduce outputs; we will not use them for model tuning.
- Audit logs of the replay operation are retained for 90 days for compliance; customers may request deletion earlier and we will follow contractual controls.

Suggested status page snippet (short)
Title: eu-west-1: intermittent structured output truncation (resolved; replay opt-in offered)
Body: On 2029-02-20 we experienced an intermittent issue affecting structured outputs for a small subset of requests in eu-west-1. The issue has been mitigated and the service is operating normally. Customers who require a forensic replay or timestamped evidence can opt in; details and a request form are linked from this status page.

Suggested customer email / post-incident summary (longer)
Subject: Update and offer: replay and evidence bundle for eu-west-1 structured-output event (Feb 20)
Hi <Customer-Name>,

We want to follow up on the recent issue in eu-west-1 that may have impacted a subset of your structured outputs. We recognize that some teams need definitive proof for audits or internal debugging, so we are offering a secure replay and timestamped evidence bundle at no charge.

What we will provide if you opt in:
- A replay of selected requests in an isolated verification environment using the same model version and runtime parameters.
- A signed evidence bundle (request logs, replay outputs, manifest).
- A short operator summary with any observed differences.

How to request a replay:
1) Reply to this email with: preferred scope (sample or full window), up to 10 request IDs or the time range, and preferred delivery method.
2) If you need redaction, indicate the fields to redact.
3) We'll confirm receipt and provide an ETA (sample: ~48 hours).

If you do not need a replay, no action is necessary. We apologize for the disruption and are available to discuss technical details or compliance implications.

Timeline (for internal reference)
- 2029-02-20 02:12 UTC — first anomaly detected in per-route alerts (inference-monitoring).
- 2029-02-20 03:02 UTC — SRE triage; identified correlation with prefix-prefetch rollout (canary signals).
- 2029-02-20 05:10 UTC — engineering rollback plan approved.
- 2029-02-20 10:20 UTC — rollback executed in eu-west-1; guard added.
- 2029-02-21 09:00 UTC — evidence collection pipeline started for impacted tenants (INC-2029-1345).

Open questions / TODOs (internal)
- Confirm default retention period for evidence bundles for enterprise customers vs. self-serve tenants. (Action: Maya)
- Legal to approve wording re: "not used for model tuning" for regions with strict ingest laws. (Action: Legal request ID LGL-2029-57)
- Need final status-page URL and short form link for customer requests (Action: Jordan to create a quick form).
- Validate that replay environment uses identical kernel/quantization profile (Action: Serving runtime; ticket SR-2029-098).

FAQ (short)
Q: Will replays change my data or models?
A: No. Replays are read-only and executed in an isolated verification environment.

Q: Do replays count against my usage?
A: No. Replays and evidence bundles related to this incident are offered at no cost.

Q: What if I want a signed attestation?
A: We can provide a signed summary; enterprise customers can request a more formal attestation (contact CS lead).

Draft internal subject lines and alt copy (pick one)
- "Offer: Replay & evidence bundle for Feb 20 eu-west-1 event"
- "Action available: opt in to replay for impacted requests (eu-west-1)"
- "Replay and timestamped evidence available for verification — eu-west-1"

Notes to draft reviewers
- Keep language low-friction; avoid heavy legalese in the initial email. Reserve formal attestation language for follow-up if requested.
- Make the request process as low-touch as possible: form -> confirm -> deliver bundle.
- Coordinate with legal before sending to EU-regulated tenants.

Attachments and links to include in final delivery
- Customer request form (short URL)
- Link to incident postmortem (internal) and a redacted public postmortem version that can be shared if requested
- Contact card for CS lead and SRE on-call

Drafts below (copyable)
Status page short body:
"On 2029-02-20 we observed intermittent truncation of structured outputs in eu-west-1 affecting a small subset of streaming sessions. The issue is mitigated. If you require a replay or a timestamped evidence bundle for audit or debugging, please follow the opt-in link."

Customer email (short):
Hi <Name>,
Following our earlier notice, we are offering a secure replay and signed evidence bundle for requests affected by the eu-west-1 structured-output issue on 2029-02-20. Reply with the request IDs or time range and we'll take it from there.

-- end of draft --

Internal references:
- INC-2029-1345 (primary incident)
- SR-2029-098 (runtime validation)
- LGL-2029-57 (legal review)

Planner notes (for finalization):
- Confirm gate for handling PII in inputs; if present we need customer-specific redaction process documented in the form.
- Ensure encryption keys used for evidence S3 links are tenant-scoped and rotate after delivery.
